tts: Someone stole our registry password and pushed their own image. Production refused it in two seconds.
Here's the problem. Kubernetes runs whatever image sits in your registry, as long as the token is valid.
So every image my pipeline builds gets signed by the release workflow itself. No private key anywhere.
Plus three signed papers: where it was built, a vulnerability scan, and a list of every library inside.
At the cluster door, Kai-verno checks all of it, before any pod can start.
Then I attack it. Seven different ways, on every single release.
An image from another registry? Refused in under half a second.
Unsigned, pushed with a stolen token? Refused in two seconds.
The scary one: a perfectly valid signature, from the wrong workflow. Still refused.
A malicious commit to git? Argo C-D applied it. The cluster refused it six seconds later.
And the real release? Admitted, every single time.
The full project is free. Follow, and I'll show you how to build it.
